headline: Thanksgiving's heavy rain eases to showers with a slight chance of thunderstorms and gusty winds through noon, while coastal flooding continues along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and outer coast until 6 PM; a lighter system brings rain Friday afternoon before a brief dry Saturday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Behind Thanksgiving morning's storm, rain turns to scattered showers with dry breaks through the afternoon, and there is a slight chance of thunderstorms (about 15 to 25 percent this morning), mainly on the Olympic Peninsula around Sequim and Port Angeles. A Wind Advisory runs until noon for the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore, the Lake Crescent area along US 101, Port Townsend and the Puget Sound lowlands including Seattle, with south to southeast gusts of about 25 to 35 mph, strongest on the coast and in the northern interior; winds ease this evening and tonight. The storm dumped 3 to 6 inches of rain on the Olympic Peninsula over the past day, sending the Skokomish River into moderate flood, near major flood stage early this morning, and it stays in flood through tonight. A Winter Storm Warning continues for the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades until 4 AM Friday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday starts quieter, then a much weaker system brings light rain back across the area by Friday afternoon, with far less rain and wind than Thursday's storm. The Skokomish River should fall below flood stage Friday, while other rivers keep rising today without more flooding expected. Saturday turns drier as a weak area of high pressure moves onshore, with temperatures back to normal for the season.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The dry break is brief: the high pressure moves east Saturday night and another storm system moves offshore Sunday, though computer models disagree widely on how it develops. One model run spins up a strong low pressure center offshore by Sunday night, which forecasters are watching because of possible holiday travel impacts. Models keep disagreeing into early next week, with a hint of another short dry break around Wednesday; for now the forecast calls for near-normal temperatures and a general chance of rain, typical for early December, and the Skokomish River could rise again next week.

coast: Coastal flooding remains a concern Thursday as very high tides combine with storm surge and high surf, with impacts peaking on the inland waters today before tides gradually weaken. A Coastal Flood Warning runs until 6 PM for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca and the northern and Grays Harbor County coasts, and until 10 AM for Puget Sound shorelines from Olympia to Whatcom County, Hood Canal and the San Juan Islands; Coastal Flood Advisories cover the Port Townsend area until 10 AM and the lower Chehalis River valley until 6 PM. Coastal Flood Watches follow for the San Juan Islands late tonight through Friday morning and the Grays Harbor County coast Friday morning through Friday evening. On the water, a Storm Warning covers the east entrance of the Strait until noon, Gale Warnings cover Admiralty Inlet and the northern inland waters until noon and the coastal waters and west entrance of the Strait until 10 AM, and Small Craft Advisories run until 7 PM for Puget Sound and Hood Canal, until 10 PM for the central and west Strait and the Grays Harbor bar, and until 4 PM Friday on the coastal waters; thunderstorms moving in from the ocean could bring lightning, gusty winds and small hail. Ocean seas of 15 to 20 feet ease to 10 to 15 feet by Friday morning and below 10 feet this weekend, though a westerly push of wind is likely through the Strait, and seas rise above 10 feet again next week.

Possible strong offshore storm Sunday night that could affect holiday travel

confidence: Confidence is good for Thursday's showers, Friday's light rain and a dry Saturday, but low from Sunday into next week because computer models disagree on the next storms.
